newsitem.title: UK: Citibank says some stolen certs resurface.
newsitem.headline: Citibank says some stolen certs resurface.

text.p: Citibank confirmed on Monday some certificates stolen in the mid-1980s had resurfaced, but said it never had a contract with a private detective to recover the securities.
Citibank said it had no material financial exposure to any of the securities.

The Evening Standard newspaper reported on Monday that the U.S. bank had retained a British private detective, Chris Morris, to recover bonds with an estimated face value of at least $111 billion stolen from a waste disposal company.

"In 1985-86 Citibank used an outside destruction firm, MSM Corp, to dispose of a number of cancelled certificates. Subsequently the bank discovered that a number of these certificates thought to have been destroyed had reappeared and some have been fraudulently presented for transfer or offered as collateral for loans," Citibank said in a statement.

"Citibank is not able to provide details of any specific joint recovery activities with the City of London Police or any other law enforcement authority. However, we strongly refute any allegation that Chris Morris had a contract with Citibank," the bank added.
The Evening Standard reported that Morris was used as part of a complex sting operation set up in 1995 by the City of London and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to recover the stolen bonds.
